events.blurb: Aymar, lord of Souvigny, is granted fiefs on the Allier River by King Charles the Simple. His son Adhémar acquires the castle of Bourbon, giving the family its name: the first record of the Bourbons.
events.label: First Bourbon fiefs, 913

events.blurb: Beatrice of Burgundy, Lady of Bourbon, marries Robert of France, Count of Clermont and son of Saint Louis. The Capetian prince and the Bourbon heiress found the royal House of Bourbon.
events.label: Robert of Clermont marries, 1272

events.blurb: King Charles IV raises Bourbonnais to a duchy for Louis I, Robert's son. The dukes of Bourbon become the first peers of the blood royal after the king's own sons.
events.label: Duchy of Bourbon, 1327

events.blurb: Charles, Constable of Bourbon, the last duke of the old line, is killed leading the imperial assault on Rome. His death ends the direct ducal line and scatters the Bourbon inheritance.
events.label: Constable dies at Rome, 1527

events.blurb: Henry of Navarre, head of the Bourbon house, becomes Henry IV of France after the Valois line dies out. The Protestant king converts, declaring Paris well worth a Mass, and ends the Wars of Religion.
events.label: Henry IV king, 1589

events.blurb: Henry IV issues the Edict of Nantes, granting French Protestants freedom of worship and fortified towns for their security. It ends thirty-six years of religious war.
events.label: Edict of Nantes, 1598

events.blurb: François Ravaillac assassinates Henry IV in Paris. The nine-year-old Louis XIII succeeds under his mother Marie de' Medici's regency, and Richelieu soon begins the work of royal absolutism.
events.label: Henry IV assassinated, 1610

events.blurb: Louis XIV, the Sun King, takes personal rule at twenty-two after Mazarin's death. His seventy-two-year reign, the longest in European history, makes Versailles the center of the continent and France the model of absolutism.
events.label: Louis XIV takes power, 1643

events.blurb: Louis XIV revokes the Edict of Nantes, outlawing Protestant worship in France. Hundreds of thousands of Huguenots flee, carrying their skills to England, Prussia, and the Netherlands.
events.label: Revocation of Nantes, 1685

events.blurb: Philip, Duke of Anjou, grandson of Louis XIV, becomes Philip V of Spain on the death of the last Habsburg king. The Bourbon dynasty takes the Spanish throne, and Europe goes to war to stop France and Spain uniting.
events.label: Philip V of Spain, 1700

events.blurb: The Treaty of Utrecht ends the War of the Spanish Succession: Philip V keeps Spain and its empire but renounces any claim to the French throne, forever separating the two Bourbon crowns.
events.label: Treaty of Utrecht, 1713

events.blurb: Louis XIV dies at Versailles after seventy-two years on the throne. His five-year-old great-grandson succeeds as Louis XV, and the regency that follows unwinds the Sun King's system.
events.label: Louis XIV dies, 1715

events.blurb: Louis XVI takes the throne, inheriting a bankrupt state and a rising demand for reform. Fifteen years later he will summon the Estates-General, and the Revolution will follow.
events.label: Louis XVI accedes, 1774

events.blurb: Parisians storm the Bastille, and the National Assembly proclaims the rights of man. The Bourbon monarchy, unchallenged for a century, collapses into revolution.
events.label: Revolution begins, 1789

events.blurb: Louis XVI is guillotined in the Place de la Révolution after a trial by the Convention. The execution makes the Revolution's break with monarchy irreversible.
events.label: Louis XVI executed, 1793

events.blurb: Napoleon's invasion of Spain forces Ferdinand VII, the Spanish Bourbon king, to abdicate at Bayonne. Madrid rises against the French on the Dos de Mayo, beginning the Peninsular War.
events.label: Ferdinand VII deposed, 1808

events.blurb: After Napoleon's fall, Louis XVI's brother returns as Louis XVIII, restored by the allies. The Bourbon Restoration tries to rule a France the Revolution remade.
events.label: Louis XVIII restored, 1814

events.blurb: Charles X, Louis XVIII's brother and an uncompromising reactionary, takes the throne and moves to restore the old order by ordinance. Six years later Paris throws him out.
events.label: Charles X accedes, 1824

events.blurb: The July Revolution deposes Charles X, and Louis-Philippe, head of the Orléans branch of the Bourbons, takes power as King of the French. The citizen-king rules for eighteen years.
events.label: Louis-Philippe king, 1830

events.blurb: Isabella II, three years old, succeeds Ferdinand VII in Spain, and her uncle Don Carlos refuses to accept a female succession. The Carlist Wars that follow divide Spain for forty years.
events.label: Isabella II accedes, 1833

events.blurb: Barricades rise across Paris, Louis-Philippe abdicates and flees to England, and the Second Republic is proclaimed. The French Bourbon monarchy ends.
events.label: Louis-Philippe falls, 1848

events.blurb: Isabella II is deposed by the Glorious Revolution and flees to France. Spain experiments with a republic, a Savoyard king, and another republic before the Bourbons return.
events.label: Isabella II deposed, 1868

events.blurb: Alfonso XII, Isabella's son, is restored to the Spanish throne, founding the Restoration system that governs Spain, with interruptions, until 1931.
events.label: Alfonso XII restored, 1874

events.blurb: Alfonso XIII leaves Spain after republican victories in municipal elections, and the Second Republic is proclaimed. The Spanish Bourbons go into exile for the second time.
events.label: Alfonso XIII exiled, 1931

events.blurb: Two days after Franco's death, Juan Carlos I, groomed by the dictator as his successor, becomes king and instead steers Spain to democracy, facing down a military coup in 1981.
events.label: Juan Carlos I king, 1975

events.blurb: Juan Carlos abdicates in favor of his son, who reigns as Felipe VI. The Bourbon dynasty, first recorded on the Allier eleven centuries earlier, still occupies the Spanish throne.
events.label: Felipe VI accedes, 2014
